observations.name: Crimson Defense CTF (CDCTF) 2026

facts.format: Virtual 12-hour collegiate-level Jeopardy CTF; teams up to four; universities may field multiple teams.
facts.categories: Reverse Engineering, Log & Network Traffic Analysis, Forensics, Password Cracking, Cryptography, Open Source Intelligence, Social Engineering, and AI.
facts.eligibility_evidence: Organizer says the competition was opened to any college student in the United States in 2025 and describes the 2026 event as collegiate-level. CTFtime currently states registration is open through September 30, 2026.
facts.prize_evidence: CTFtime currently lists trophies for the top three teams if US-based; no cash prize was verified.
facts.rules_boundary: Organizer explicitly prohibits attacking the CDCTF platform, brute-forcing, automated tools against hosted challenges unless specified, receiving help from non-team members, cross-team flag/solution sharing, sabotage, multiple accounts, automated submissions, and sharing competition materials during the event.
facts.authorization_boundary: Authorization is limited to organizer-issued competition challenges under the current rules. Public Crimson Defense/University of Alabama systems, unrelated hosts, accounts, networks, repositories, and third-party services are not testing targets.

missing_verification: Open the current Google registration form directly and preserve its exact September 30 cutoff/timezone, required participant fields, capacity, and acceptance state.
Confirm whether 2026 eligibility is exactly all U.S. college students or has school/enrollment/residency restrictions beyond the organizer page wording.
Verify entry cost; the organizer page does not publish a fee.
Verify current award/trophy terms from organizer-primary rules rather than relying on the CTFtime prize field.
Preserve any platform-specific challenge rules, permitted-tool exceptions, scoring details, and participant-specific registration/team state before active work.
observations.deduplication: No CDCTF research item was identified in inspected current-main coordination state or open research PR titles/bodies. This maps to the existing ctftime-upcoming discovery lane and does not create a competing recurring source registry.
observations.recommended_next_action: Because registration closes imminently, reopen the organizer registration form and rules before the deadline. If participant eligibility and registration intent are established, create a structured CTF case limited to organizer-issued challenges; otherwise preserve this as lifecycle/source-health evidence only.
